s: A scrum master reports that the product owner is unavailable for most of the iteration, so the team guesses at acceptance criteria and rework is rising. What is the BEST action for the project manager?
o: Ask the team to pause work on unclear stories until the product owner is free
Show the rework cost and agree a set availability pattern or an empowered delegate
Appoint a team member as proxy product owner to settle acceptance questions
Move all acceptance reviews to the end of the release so the team is not blocked
e: The fix is to restore access to a decision maker with authority. A proxy without authority changes nothing, and waiting or deferring acceptance increases risk.

s: Two functional managers argue over whose department's engineer should lead a design review. Each says the other's engineer lacks the skills. What do you do FIRST?
o: Lead the design review yourself so neither department's engineer is favoured
Select the engineer with the longer record of experience and inform both managers
Convene both managers and agree the lead against criteria the review requires
Ask the sponsor to choose between the two engineers before any discussion
e: Facilitate a decision based on agreed criteria before escalating.

s: A team member asks for training on a tool that is not needed for the current phase but will be in two phases' time. What is the BEST response?
o: Decline for now and revisit the request once the later phase gets closer
Add it to the team development plan and schedule it before the skill is needed
Recruit someone who already knows the tool in time for the later phase
Let them study it on their own time and reimburse any course fee later
e: Developing skills ahead of need is part of resource planning and team development.

s: A new executive joins the steering committee, and her expectations differ sharply from the original charter. What should you do?
o: Meet her, assess the gap against the charter and take changes through governance
Revise the plan now to reflect her expectations, since she sits on the steering committee
Wait until she raises a formal change request before taking any action
Send her the approved charter and explain that the baseline is already agreed
e: Engage the new stakeholder, analyse the gap, and route changes through governance.

s: Your team is demotivated after a long period of overtime. What is the MOST effective leadership action?
o: Ask the team for patience until the next release milestone is delivered
Rotate fresh members onto the team to share out the remaining workload
Cut the overload, recognise the effort and let the team shape a sustainable pace
Pay a one-off bonus to thank everyone for the overtime they have worked
e: Address the root cause, which is workload, and involve the team in the fix.

s: A stakeholder is annoyed that they hear about issues late. Which is the BEST improvement?
o: Copy them on every project email and log entry so that nothing is missed
Hold a daily meeting with them to review all emerging issues and risks
Apologise and promise to inform them sooner without changing the process
Agree which issues need immediate notice, by what channel, and update the plan
e: Right information to the right person at the right time. Agree the triggers and channel.

s: You are asked by a senior executive to remove a risk from the register because it makes the project look bad. The risk is real. What do you do?
o: Reclassify it as an issue so the register no longer shows it as a risk
Move it to a separate working file and keep the register for approved items
Keep the risk, explain it with the response plan and escalate if pressure continues
Remove it as asked, and record the executive's instruction in your project notes
e: Honesty and transparency. Do not delete valid risks; explain, offer a plan and escalate if needed.

s: A hybrid team's predictive subproject leader says the agile team's lack of detailed estimates makes planning impossible. What is the BEST approach?
o: Ask the agile team to produce full detailed estimates for the whole scope up front
Move the agile team to the predictive method so both follow one planning process
Have the predictive leader plan with allowances and ignore the agile team's work
Agree release-level estimates and a rolling forecast for the predictive plan
e: Tailor planning interfaces so each approach works and they integrate at agreed points.

s: Which activity BEST helps establish a common vision at the start of a project?
o: Emailing the approved charter to every team member and stakeholder
A kickoff or visioning workshop with the team and key stakeholders
Publishing the baselined schedule and milestone plan to all stakeholders
Assigning individual work packages and tasks to each team member
e: Collaborative sessions build shared understanding better than one-way communication.

s: The customer's expectations of release timing rose after a competitor's announcement. The plan does not support the earlier date. What do you do?
o: Commit to the earlier date and look for ways to recover the time later
Tell the customer the earlier date is not possible under the current plan
Ask the team to work sustained overtime until the earlier date is met
Lay out the trade-offs and agree a realistic date through change control
e: Manage expectations with options and facts, not promises you cannot keep.

s: A project has two paths: A-B-D with a 14-day duration and A-C-D with 12 days. Activity B is delayed by 3 days. What is the new project duration?
o: 14 days
17 days
15 days
12 days
e: The path A-B-D becomes 17 days and remains the longest.

s: A project has CPI 1.05 and SPI 0.85. Which statement is MOST accurate?
o: Under budget but behind schedule
Over budget and ahead of schedule
Over budget and behind schedule
Under budget and ahead of schedule
e: CPI above 1 is under budget. SPI below 1 is behind schedule.

s: BAC is $600,000, EV $300,000, AC $360,000. What is the estimate to complete (ETC) if future work will run at the current cost efficiency?
e: CPI = 300/360 = 0.833. EAC = BAC/CPI = $720,000. ETC = EAC − AC = $360,000. $720,000 is the EAC, not the ETC.

s: A risk with a 40% probability and a $100,000 impact has a mitigation that costs $30,000 and cuts the probability to 10%. What is the net benefit of mitigation?
e: EMV before = $40,000; after = $10,000, so mitigation saves $30,000. It costs $30,000, so the net benefit is $0: not worth doing on cost alone.

s: Which tool decomposes the project scope into smaller manageable deliverables?
o: Resource breakdown structure
Gantt chart schedule view
Work breakdown structure
Risk breakdown structure
e: The WBS decomposes the total scope hierarchically.

s: A team's lead time for items is 15 days but the cycle time is 4 days. What does this suggest?
o: The team is slow once it starts an item, so review skills and tooling
Quality is poor and items return for rework, so tighten the definition of done
Items wait long before work starts, so examine the queue and prioritisation
Estimates are inflated, so ask the team to re-estimate its backlog items
e: The gap between lead time and cycle time is waiting time before work starts.

s: You must decide whether to add a quality inspection step. Which analysis BEST helps?
o: Resource histogram of tester capacity compared with the inspection workload
Cost of quality, weighing prevention and appraisal against failure costs
Stakeholder analysis of which groups would prefer additional inspection steps
Critical path analysis to see whether the inspection would delay the schedule
e: Cost of quality weighs the cost of conformance against the cost of non-conformance.

s: A time-and-materials contract has no cap and the seller's hours are rising faster than progress. What is the BEST step?
o: Review hours against progress and negotiate a not-to-exceed cap or new arrangement
Ask the team to track the seller's hours informally and report concerns later
Keep paying invoices as submitted and settle any disputes at contract close
Terminate the contract for convenience and re-tender the remaining work
e: Administer the contract actively and seek a formal control such as a cap.

s: Which tool shows who is accountable, responsible, consulted and informed for each task?
o: Organisation breakdown structure of reporting lines
RACI chart (responsibility assignment matrix)
Network diagram of task dependencies and sequence
Resource histogram of staffing levels over time
e: A RACI chart is a responsibility assignment matrix.

s: Status reports show progress as green for six weeks, but the team says they are struggling. What is the BEST action?
o: Ask the status reporter for more detailed weekly reports to confirm progress
Accept the green status, since it follows the approved reporting format
Talk with the team and check actual progress against how status is measured
Replace the status reporter with someone who can give a more accurate view
e: Verify with data and direct conversation when signals conflict. Evaluate project status honestly.

s: An approved change adds a feature that touches scope, schedule, cost and risk. What is the BEST way to keep the plans consistent?
o: Update the plan and baselines together through integrated change control
Record the change in the change log and update plans at the next review
Update only the schedule baseline, since it is the one most affected
Have each plan owner update their own plan as time allows over the next weeks
e: Integrated change control keeps the baselines and subsidiary plans consistent.

s: Which activity belongs to project closure?
o: Developing the project charter and appointing the sponsor
Defining detailed scope and agreeing requirements with stakeholders
Archiving project information and releasing resources
Creating the work breakdown structure and the schedule baseline
e: Closure includes final acceptance, lessons learned, archiving and releasing resources.

s: A team wants to add a new tool mid-iteration that would speed testing but needs a week to learn. What do you recommend?
o: Trial it as a time-boxed experiment or adopt it at the next iteration boundary
Adopt it immediately and absorb the learning week into the current iteration
Rule out any new tools until the end of the project to protect velocity
Let one member learn it alongside normal tasks without telling the product owner
e: Protect the iteration commitment, then use a deliberate experiment.

s: The project is 30% complete and has spent 45% of its budget. The sponsor asks you for an updated forecast. What should you give?
o: The remaining unspent budget, presented as the amount available to finish
A forecast based on performance to date, with stated assumptions and options
The original budget as approved, since no change request has been raised
An estimate drawn from similar past projects, without current performance data
e: Provide an EAC with assumptions and options. CPI is below 1 here so the forecast exceeds the original.

s: The PMO changes its reporting template mid-project. Your project's governance already has agreed reports. What should you do?
o: Report in both formats for the rest of the project to satisfy everyone
Keep the already agreed reports, since governance was set at project start
Review the template, agree with PMO and sponsor how to meet it and update the plans
Let the team choose whichever format they prefer for each reporting period
e: Align governance with the organisation's requirements through agreement and plan updates.

s: An auditor finds that your team has not retained approvals for three changes. What is the BEST response?
o: Acknowledge the gap, recover what evidence you can and fix the process
Argue that the approvals were given verbally and rely on witness statements
Treat it as a minor record gap and plan to correct it before the next audit
Have the board re-approve the three changes now and file the new approvals
e: Be transparent, fix the process, and keep records. Records are part of compliance.

s: A supply shortage in a key component raises costs and delays delivery for all vendors. Your project depends on that component. What do you do FIRST?
o: Hold current activities until suppliers confirm when the component will be available
Recommend cancelling the project, since every vendor faces the same shortage
Place a large advance order for the component now to secure your supply
Assess impact on schedule, cost and benefits and take options to the sponsor
e: External environment changes require impact assessment and a decision through governance.

s: After go-live, adoption is only 30% of the target. The system works as specified. What should you do?
o: Close the project as planned, since the system meets the agreed specification
Report the low adoption as a user training failure to be fixed by the business
Investigate barriers with users and agree a remedy with the sponsor
Declare the delivery a success, since acceptance testing passed in full
e: Value comes from adoption. Work with the business owner to remove barriers.

s: A risk trigger occurs, but the response owner is on leave and no alternate is named. What should you do?
o: Wait for the owner to return from leave, since they know the response best
Run the response through an alternate, then name alternates for every response
Log the trigger as an issue and ask the owner to act on return from leave
Note the trigger and watch it, as the risk has not yet become an issue
e: Act on the trigger now, then fix the gap in the plan.
